title: Signed cubical partition boundary expansion and paired faces
statement:
Let $r\geq0$, $D=\mathbf Z^r$, and $u_1,\ldots,u_r$ be its ordered standard basis. For each integer $a$, let $C_a$ be the free abelian group on $[v,I]$, where $v\in D$ and $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ has cardinality $a$, and zero when $a<0$ or $a>r$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Use the cubical differential of [lem-sfb-integral-lattice-cubical-contraction], explicitly
$$d[v,I]=\sum_{i\in I}(-1)^{\#\{j\in I:j<i\}}([v+u_i,I\setminus\{i\}]-[v,I\setminus\{i\}]),$$
with $d=0$ on $C_0$. Write $u_A=\sum_{a\in A}u_a$, $\epsilon(A,C)=(-1)^{\#\{(a,c)\in A\times C:c<a\}}$, and in the total graded tensor group $T_n=\bigoplus_{a+b=n}C_a\otimes_{\mathbf Z}C_b$ put
$$d_T(x\otimes y)=dx\otimes y+(-1)^a x\otimes dy\quad(x\in C_a),\qquad P(v,I)=\sum_{A\sqcup C=I}\epsilon(A,C)[v,A]\otimes[v+u_A,C].$$
Here the tensors and chain-complex terminology are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. For $i\in I$ and an ordered disjoint partition $B\sqcup C=I\setminus\{i\}$ define
$$p=\#\{b\in B:b<i\},\quad q=\#\{c\in C:c<i\},\quad t=\#\{b\in B:i<b\},\quad N=\#\{(b,c)\in B\times C:c<b\}.$$
The first-factor face indexed by $i$ in the summand $(B\cup\{i\},C)$ has coefficient
$$(-1)^{N+q+p}=s,\qquad s=(-1)^{p+q}\epsilon(B,C),$$
and the second-factor face indexed by $i$ in $(B,C\cup\{i\})$, including the tensor differential sign, has coefficient
$$(-1)^{N+t+|B|+q}=s.$$
More precisely these two face contributions to $d_TP(v,I)$ are respectively
$$s\bigl([v+u_i,B]\otimes[v+u_B+u_i,C]-[v,B]\otimes[v+u_B+u_i,C]\bigr)$$
and
$$s\bigl([v,B]\otimes[v+u_B+u_i,C]-[v,B]\otimes[v+u_B,C]\bigr).$$
The indexing of all first-factor faces by $(i,B,C)$ and all second-factor faces by $(i,B,C)$ is bijective in each case. The explicit boundary expansion is:
$$d_TP(v,I)=\sum_{i\in I}\ \sum_{B\sqcup C=I\setminus\{i\}}(-1)^{\#\{j\in I:j<i\}}\epsilon(B,C)\bigl([v+u_i,B]\otimes[v+u_i+u_B,C]-[v,B]\otimes[v+u_B,C]\bigr).$$
For $I=\varnothing$ this is the equality $0=0$.

proof.text: The first indexing map is $(A,C,i)\mapsto(i,A\setminus\{i\},C)$, with inverse $(i,B,C)\mapsto(B\cup\{i\},C,i)$. The second is $(A,C,i)\mapsto(i,A,C\setminus\{i\})$, with inverse $(i,B,C)\mapsto(B,C\cup\{i\},i)$. Disjointness gives $i\notin B\cup C$, so removing after inserting, and inserting after removing, recover both indices. Thus each map is a bijection onto the triples in the statement.

proof.text: Fix such a triple. Counting the elements below $i$ gives $\#\{j\in I:j<i\}=p+q$, and splitting $B$ below and above $i$ gives $|B|=p+t$. The inversion pairs for $(B\cup\{i\},C)$ consist of the $N$ old pairs and the $q$ pairs $(i,c)$ with $c<i$. The position of $i$ in $B\cup\{i\}$ is $p$. Hence the first-face coefficient is $(-1)^{N+q+p}=(-1)^{p+q}\epsilon(B,C)=s$.

proof.text: For $(B,C\cup\{i\})$ the new inversion pairs are precisely the $t$ pairs $(b,i)$ with $i<b$. The position of $i$ in $C\cup\{i\}$ is $q$, and the tensor sign is $(-1)^{|B|}$. Thus the second coefficient is $(-1)^{N+t+|B|+q}=(-1)^{N+p+q+2t}=s$, since $(-1)^{2t}=1$ in $\mathbf Z$.

proof.text: Unfold the definitions of the two signed faces. In the first face, the sum of directions of insert i B is u_i+u_B because i is absent from B; removing i recovers B. In the second face, removing i from insert i C recovers C. Substitute the two coefficient equalities already proved. Associativity and commutativity of lattice addition identify their middle tensor. This gives the two displayed local face identities, and their sum is s times (x-y)+(y-z)=x-z.

proof.text: For each B subset I.erase i set C=I.erase i\B. It is disjoint from B with union I.erase i, so apply the proved local sign and face identities. Rewrite the sum of its two scalar multiples as the scalar multiple of the sum. The identical middle tensors cancel by (x-y)+(y-z)=x-z. Filter the disjoint union B union C=I.erase i below i: because i<i is false, its cardinality is the cardinality of I filtered below i. Thus p+q is the position of i in I. Commutativity and associativity of lattice addition put the translated vertex in the requested order. Equality of summands proves equality of the two finite sums. For I empty the resulting outer sum is empty, giving the final zero clause without any separate differential calculation.
